subject: Information Theory
title: Matched Filters
description: A micro-lesson that makes Matched Filters usable.

hook.text: Radar knows the exact pulse it sent. The optimal receiver is a filter shaped exactly like that pulse.

buildup.text: A matched filter maximizes SNR at the output by correlating the received signal with the known transmitted shape.

discovery.text: The math proves it: no other filter can achieve a higher peak SNR at the detection moment.

twist.text: The matched filter is optimal only for known signals in white noise. Real-world noise requires modifications.

climax.text: Radar, sonar, GPS, and digital communication receivers all use matched filtering as their foundation.

punchline.text: Know what you sent. Build a filter that listens for exactly that.

quiz.question: What does a matched filter maximize?
